title: Avant, devant, de neuf heures à midi
summary: Separate time from physical position and describe travel, intervals and punctuality.
objectives: Use monter dans and descendre de for transport.
State timetable intervals, next/last periods and punctuality accurately.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Earlier is not the same as in front
paragraphs: Avant and après usually order events in time: avant le repas, après le cours. Devant and derrière locate things physically: devant la porte, derrière le bâtiment. There are extended sequence uses of avant/après, but a simple physical location normally needs devant/derrière.

For getting on or into a vehicle use monter dans; for getting off or out use descendre de. Contract de with articles: du bus, du train, de la voiture, de l'autobus. Monter sur means onto the surface, appropriate for mounting a bicycle or getting onto a roof, not an ordinary passenger entering a bus.
points: Present movement: je monte dans le bus. Completed movement: je suis monté/montée dans le bus. Moving an object uses a different construction: j'ai monté les valises.

examples.english: Wait in front of the pharmacy, not behind it.

examples.french: Nous **descendons du** bus près du parc.
examples.english: We get off the bus near the park.

sections.title: Name the interval and the reference point
paragraphs: Use de ... à ... for an interval: de neuf heures à midi, du lundi au vendredi, du 3 au 6 juin. A starting expression with depuis can pair with jusqu'à, but de ... à is the compact timetable pattern here. Do not combine de with jusqu'à merely by copying two different templates unless the intended emphasis calls for it.

Tôt/tard mean early/late in the day or relative to an activity. En avance/en retard compare with an expected time; à l'heure means on time. Precisely state an amount with cinq minutes d'avance/de retard, or en avance/en retard de cinq minutes.

Place prochain/dernier after a named calendar period when relating it to now: lundi prochain, la semaine dernière, le mois prochain, l'année dernière. Before a noun, they can select an item in a sequence: la prochaine séance, les trois derniers jours. La prochaine fois and la dernière fois are normal fixed combinations. Prochain/dernier agree with the noun.
points: Tard does not necessarily mean late for an appointment: un train à minuit peut être à l'heure. A late evening departure can still be punctual.

examples.french: Le guichet ouvre **de neuf heures à midi**, **du mardi au samedi**.
examples.english: The counter opens from nine to noon, from Tuesday to Saturday.
examples.note: Time and weekday intervals use different article contractions.

examples.french: Le cours a lieu **du 4 au 8 octobre**.
examples.english: The course takes place from October 4 to October 8.

examples.french: Le train part tard, mais il est **à l'heure** ; nous avons **dix minutes d'avance**.
examples.english: The train leaves late in the day, but it is on time; we are ten minutes early.

examples.french: La semaine **dernière**, nous avons réservé ; **la prochaine séance** est lundi **prochain**.
examples.english: Last week, we booked; the next session is next Monday.
examples.note: Calendar reference versus the next event in a sequence.

mistakes.avoid: Le bureau ouvre de lundi à le vendredi.
mistakes.prefer: Le bureau ouvre du lundi au vendredi.
mistakes.why: A recurring weekday range uses de + le and à + le contractions.

practice.prompt: Supply avant or devant for time: Je téléphone ___ le dîner.
practice.explanation: The call happens earlier than dinner.

practice.prompt: Supply après or derrière for physical position: Le jardin est ___ la maison.
practice.explanation: The garden is physically behind the house.

practice.prompt: Supply dans or sur for a passenger entering: Elle monte ___ le train.
Complete the interval: Le centre ouvre de huit heures ___ dix-huit heures.
practice.explanation: The time interval uses de ... à.

practice.prompt: Supply du or dans le: Nous descendons ___ métro.
Supply avant or devant for physical location: Je vous attends ___ l'entrée.
Supply du or de: Le stage dure ___ 12 au 15 mai.
Supply au or à: Le bureau ouvre du lundi ___ jeudi.
Supply en avance or en retard: Appointment at 10:00, arrival at 10:12. Je suis ___.
practice.explanation: Arrival is after the expected time.

practice.prompt: Supply the exact-time expression: Appointment at 14:00, arrival at 14:00. Je suis ___.
practice.explanation: The arrival matches the appointment time.

practice.prompt: Agree prochain: Nous partons la semaine ___.
practice.explanation: Feminine calendar period, after the noun.

practice.prompt: Agree dernier: Elle est venue l'année ___.
Supply the phrase for a five-minute delay: Le bus a cinq minutes ___.
Supply prochaine or prochain: La ___ fois, appelle avant de venir.
practice.explanation: La prochaine fois is feminine and places prochaine before fois.

practice.prompt: Supply après or derrière for time: Nous discutons ___ le cours.
practice.explanation: The conversation is later than the class.

practice.prompt: A train scheduled for 23:50 leaves at 23:50. Which statement is accurate?
choices: Il part tard, mais il est à l'heure.
answers: Il part tard, mais il est à l'heure.
practice.explanation: Late in the day does not mean late for the schedule.

production_task.prompt: Give someone directions for attending a short course: dates, hours, where to get off and where to wait.
production_task.model_answer: Le cours a lieu du 6 au 9 avril, de neuf heures à midi. Descendez du bus devant la mairie. Attendez devant l'entrée principale. Essayez d'arriver avec cinq minutes d'avance.
production_task.translation: The course takes place from April 6 to April 9, from nine to noon. Get off the bus in front of city hall. Wait in front of the main entrance. Try to arrive five minutes early.
rubric: Use correct date and time interval contractions.
Separate before in time from in front of in space.
Use de for getting off a vehicle.
